meta.title: Views of communist Poland
meta.question: Do Poles look back on communist Poland (the PRL) favourably?
meta.measure: Average view of communist Poland, from 0 (very negative) to 10 (very positive)
meta.anchor: Pooled from every question on views of communist Poland (the PRL) and of life then, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: How satisfied were you with the way the communist regime worked? (1 completely dissatisfied ... 10 completely satisfied)
items.notes: CDCEE January 1991 and March 2000. In 2000, respondents too young to judge (96) have no position.

items.wording: Which comes closest to your view of communism as a form of government? (the worst form; bad but no worse than some others; all right for some countries; a good form of government)
items.notes: PGSS 1992-2010 (10 waves); the GSS question. Communism in general rather than the PRL, but in Poland the two go together (r = 0.33-0.49 with PGSS's for/against socialism question).

items.wording: Did the socialist system (regime) in Poland bring more gains or more losses? (only gains ... only losses)
items.notes: POLPAN 1988, 1993, 1998, 2003, 2008, 2013, 2018: the one question in every POLPAN wave. In 1988 it judges the system then in place. In 2013 the regex takes B01.a (whole sample) and not the duplicate P4 of the supplementary questionnaire.

items.wording: Looking back, was the decision to introduce martial law (1981) right or wrong? (definitely right ... definitely wrong)
items.notes: CBOS 1994-12, 1996-11, 2001-11, 2011-11, 2014-06, 2016-11. A judgement on the communist authorities' central decision rather than on the PRL as a whole; see the notes.

items.wording: Did the socialist system bring most people in Poland more gains or more losses? (only gains ... only losses)
items.notes: CBOS 1996-09, 1998-05, 1999-04, 2004-05, 2005-08. The same question as POLPAN's.

items.wording: If there had been no socialism and Poland had had capitalism for 45 years after the war, would people in Poland now live much better, a bit better, the same, a bit worse or much worse? (much worse = 10)
items.notes: CBOS 1997-05 (codes out of order: 5 = the same). The version about people in Poland; the one about the respondent's own family is not used.

items.wording: Did the socialist system bring most people more gains, more losses, or as many of each? (codes out of order)
How would you rate the political system as it was before (under communism)? (1 very bad ... 10 very good)
As above, codes in order (much better ... much worse)
items.notes: CBOS 1998-05; the version about people in Poland.

items.wording: How would you rate the political system as it was in the past (under communism)? (1 bad ... 10 very good)
Did the socialist system bring most people more gains than losses, as many gains as losses, or more losses than gains?
How do you assess the PRL period in Polish history? (as above, codes in reverse order)
items.notes: CBOS 2000-01, where code 1 is "definitely negatively"; a separate item because the codes run the other way.

items.wording: Is communism a good idea? (yes, undecided, no)
Overall evaluation of the PRL (very good, good, bad, very bad)
How do you assess the PRL period in Polish history? (definitely positively; rather positively, though some things negatively; rather negatively, though some things positively; definitely negatively)
Overall evaluation of the PRL (clearly negative ... clearly positive; the middle is "had good and bad sides")
